mechanics.name: Run
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Every level is crossed on foot; there is no auto-run.
mechanics.summary: Harvey runs left and right, turning on the spot, with footsteps and dust in step with his speed.
how: The horizontal axis sets Harvey's run speed directly: there is no acceleration curve, so he starts and stops at once and turns by flipping.
Footstep sounds and running dust follow the distance travelled, and stop while he is mounted, airborne or dashing.
On the Spirit Fox mount he runs faster (the Summoning Talisman's speed scale).
mechanics.purpose: Getting through every level, lining up stomps and dodging boss attacks.

mechanics.name: Jump
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Gaps, ledges and stomps all start with a jump.
mechanics.summary: One press is always the same jump, with a quarter-second of coyote time after running off a ledge.
how: A press (never a hold) launches Harvey at the normal jump speed, whatever skills are learned.
Coyote time: for 0.25 s after leaving a ledge a press still counts as a jump from the ground.
A jump can't be relaunched while it is still rising, so a quick second press is free for the Super Jump or the Double Jump.
mechanics.purpose: Crossing gaps, climbing, starting stomps and clearing low boss attacks (the Landshark's fin, Sumaria's slash, the Void Shrine's swipe).

implementation.note: CharJump (SUPERTAP: one press is the normal jump)

mechanics.name: Stomp
mechanics.frequencyWhy: The main way to beat enemies in every zone and the usual way to hit a boss in its opening.
mechanics.summary: Land on an enemy from above to hit it and bounce off. Tougher zones need more stomps per enemy.
how: A stomp box under Harvey's feet only exists during a real fall (faster than a minimum speed, and not while knocked back), so standing next to an enemy never stomps it.
Each stomp deals 1 damage plus the Stomp Power skill level. Enemies take more hits zone by zone: 1 in Grassy Green, 2 in the Old Tomb and Sandy Dunes, 3 in Japan (the Japan guard 4).
When a stomp and a body touch land on the same physics step, the stomp wins (STOMPTIE).
Every enemy stomp, and every boss stomp in an opening, builds the combo.

inputs.keyboard: Jump, then fall onto the enemy
inputs.gamepad: Jump, then fall onto the enemy

mechanics.purpose: Defeating enemies, hitting bosses during openings and building the combo.

unlock.text: Available from the start; Stomp Power I-III raises its damage.

implementation.note: stomp box and the stomp-wins tie rule

mechanics.name: Health, hits and knockback
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Every enemy touch, trap and boss attack goes through it.
mechanics.summary: Three health segments on the HUD. A hit costs one, knocks Harvey back and gives him a moment of invincibility.
how: Harvey starts a level with three health segments (GameSession.StartingLives).
A hit knocks him back and takes control away until he lands; while he flickers he can't be hit again.
A hit also breaks the combo.
Ghosts hurt without knocking him back; the Healing Stone's shield and Spirit Dash's immunity stop hits altogether.
Spirit Peaches from chests give a segment back; the Healing Stone refills the bar.
mechanics.purpose: The cost of mistakes, and what the rank's survival score is measured from.

mechanics.name: Spirit Dash
mechanics.frequencyWhy: The starting attack talisman, equipped from a new game and needed for the dash-chain sections; it drains chi fast, which limits it.
mechanics.summary: Hold to dash along the ground at about 3.6x run speed. Enemies in the way are knocked out and can't hurt Harvey.
how: A talisman held in a slot: holding the button keeps the 0.5 s dash going (it retriggers while held) at 20 chi per second.
While dashing Harvey can't be hurt by enemies and defeats any he touches (traits EnemyImmunity and DefeatsEnemiesOnContact). Dash Power I-III raises its damage to 3/4/5 and its length by 12% a level.
Each enemy defeated by the dash builds the combo; the afterimages take the combo stage's colours.
The samurai monkey blocks a dash from the front (see Dash Clash).
The asset still lists Z4A1-Z4A3 as scenes where it is blocked; those scenes are no longer in the project.
mechanics.purpose: Clearing lines of enemies, building long combos and hitting bosses in their openings.

unlock.text: Equipped from a new game (starting loadout).

mechanics.name: Coins
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Laid in lines and stacks along the route of most levels.
mechanics.summary: Coins line the routes. They buy food in village shops and count toward each level's rank.
how: Touching a coin collects it; the HUD keeps the count and saves carry it.
Chests can burst coins out in an arc; those can't be collected until they land.
The rainbow combo stage pulls nearby coins in (CoinAttractor).
mechanics.purpose: Currency for village shops and 15 of the 100 rank points (the share of the level's coins collected).

mechanics.name: Chi
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Every talisman, mount and dragon flight spends it.
mechanics.summary: A 90-point pool shown as nine units in three tiers (blue, green, red). Talismans spend it; with none left, no talisman can start.
how: Full chi is 90: nine units of 10. Blue goes first, then green, then red.
Each talisman spends chi at its own rate; the dragon flies on it.
Chi comes back from Chi Crystals, chi stones in levels, chi tea and respawning.
Combo stages make talismans cheaper (to 60%, 35%, 15%, 5%, then free at the rainbow stage), and Chi Focus cuts costs by 15% / 30%.
mechanics.purpose: The resource that limits Spirit Dash, healing and mounts, so the combo and chi pickups matter.

mechanics.name: Checkpoints and respawn
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Placed in most action levels; pits and kill planes send Harvey back to them.
mechanics.summary: Touching a checkpoint opens it (flash, sparks, chime) and makes it Harvey's respawn point. Falling into a pit brings him back there.
how: A checkpoint switches to its open sprite the first time Harvey touches it, with a flash and a burst of sparks.
Kill planes and pits respawn him at the last checkpoint (or the level's respawn point).
Respawning resets enemies, falling tiles, boulder traps and boss fights (ResetOnRespawn, LevelManager.Respawned).
mechanics.purpose: Keeps long levels fair and resets traps so they can be tried again.

mechanics.name: Level goal and ranks
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Once per level cleared.
mechanics.summary: Each level ends at its treasure and is graded S, A, B, C or D from survival, time, enemies, coins and best combo.
how: Touching the treasure ends an action level; in a boss arena Harvey takes it with the action button, so he can open the boss chests first.
The grade is out of 100: survival 30, time 25 (full marks at or under par), enemies defeated 20, coins collected 15, best combo 10.
Par is worked out from the route length; a level can override it.
An S rank glows on the zone map.
mechanics.purpose: A clear end to each level and a reason to replay it well.

mechanics.name: Combo
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Any two stomp or dash defeats within 5 s start one; the dash-chain sections are built around it.
mechanics.summary: Stomps and dash defeats share one combo. Each hit inside a 5-second window raises the stage, shown as a coloured outline and swirling motes.
how: Built only by successful hits: enemy stomps, dash defeats and boss hits in openings. Ordinary jumps, bounces and dashes don't count.
Any hit within 5 s of the last moves it up a stage. The window running out, or Harvey being hurt, ends it.
Stage colours: 1 yellow, 2 orange, 3 hot pink, 4 violet, 5 rainbow. The outline glows and pulses faster each stage and blinks through the last second as a warning.
Without Combo Mastery the combo stays at stage 1; each Combo Mastery level opens the next stage.
Higher stages make talismans cheaper. The best chain counts toward the rank.
mechanics.purpose: Rewards chaining enemies, feeds chi back (with Chi Flow) and gives the game its signature visuals.

unlock.text: Stage 1 from the start; stages 2-5 with Combo Mastery I-IV.

mechanics.presenceNote: Added at runtime by the player's code, not placed in scenes.

mechanics.name: Boss openings
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Every boss fight runs on it; there is one boss per zone plus the Sandy Dunes mini-boss.
mechanics.summary: Bosses can only be hurt while slumped in an opening. Hitting one at any other time hurts Harvey instead.
how: Each boss telegraphs an attack; a miss or an over-commit leaves it dazed, belly-up or knocked over: the opening.
A stomp or a Spirit Dash in the opening takes a life; outside it the boss counters.
Each boss has its own lives and stages; later stages are faster with shorter tells.
Harvey respawning resets the fight. On defeat, three to six treasure chests drop into the arena, more for a faster win (by the level clock).
mechanics.purpose: Gives every boss the same readable rule: watch, dodge, punish.

unlock.text: Met at the end of each zone.

mechanics.name: Patrolling enemies
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Every action level has them.
mechanics.summary: Enemies patrol set paths and hurt on touch. Each zone has its own cast: Shadow Foxes, baby sand sharks, Yokai warriors and spirit ghosts.
how: A patrol path (MovingTiles) moves the enemy back and forth; touching it hurts Harvey.
Stomp or dash them; the stomps they take rise zone by zone.

Shadow Fox (Old Tomb), Baby Sand Shark and Baby Shark (Sandy Dunes), Yokai Warrior, Yokai Mount and bouncing spirit ghosts (Japan) all use this base. The Spirit Fox, the ghoul and the samurai monkey add their own behaviour (see their entries).
mechanics.purpose: The everyday threat, and what stomps, dashes and combos are spent on.

mechanics.name: Spike traps and spike rhythms
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Spike prefabs are placed in 15 build scenes; three Tomb levels run them on shared rhythms.
mechanics.summary: Spikes on floors, ceilings and walls. In the Old Tomb they pop out and sink back on a shared beat, with a peek and a rattle as the tell.
how: A spike's collider only hurts while it is at least half out, so a retracted spike is safe to cross.
A SpikeRhythm drives a group on one beat, each spike at its own phase: a few pixels' peek and a rattle, then out, then back into the stone.
Each spike can be switched to stay fully out (the per-spike toggle).
mechanics.purpose: Timing challenges and route pressure, especially Z1A6's floor and ceiling corridor.

mechanics.name: Talisman Holder and slots
mechanics.frequencyWhy: The three equipped talismans are pressed throughout play; the loadout is changed between levels.
mechanics.summary: Three talisman slots on Z, X and C. Equip talismans in the Talisman Holder, or flick slot 1 to the next one with L2.
how: Each slot's talisman starts on a press (or a hold), runs for its duration, then cools down. Chi pays for it.
The Talisman Holder (pause menu) swaps which owned talismans are equipped.
L2 / V cycles slot 1 straight to the next owned talisman not in slots 2 or 3; its HUD gem takes the new colour.
Shipping talismans: Water Breathing and Spirit Dash (starting loadout), the Healing Stone and the Summoning Talisman (boss rewards).
mechanics.purpose: Lets the player build a loadout for each level and boss.

unlock.text: Two talismans equipped from a new game; more from bosses.

mechanics.name: Treasure chests
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Usually one or two per level, plus the boss chests.
mechanics.summary: Press Up or E at a chest to open it. Rewards spring out and streak into Harvey; some chests are trapped.
how: A chest first rolls for a trap, then picks a reward by weight: a Spirit Peach (a health segment), a Chi Crystal, a gem or a burst of coins.
Trapped chests shake and knock Harvey back.
Boss chests and the challenge-room chest are never traps; the challenge chest always holds a Spirit Peach and Chi Crystals.
mechanics.purpose: The source of gems for the skill tree, and of healing and chi mid-level.

mechanics.name: Jump Mushrooms, bounce clouds and jump boxes
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Grassy Green's climbing routes are built on them; jump boxes also appear in the Dunes and Japan.
mechanics.summary: Land on a mushroom cap, a cloud or a jump box and it springs Harvey high into the air.
how: Jump Mushrooms stand on the ground; Floating Mushrooms drift. Only a landing on the cap counts (the stomp box coming down on top), so walking into the side does nothing.
Caps and clouds squash and spring back in whole art pixels, with spores or cloud puffs.
Bounces never count toward the combo, the rank or the enemy pointer.
mechanics.purpose: Vertical routes and shortcuts, especially in Grassy Green's sky levels.

mechanics.name: Off-screen enemy pointer
mechanics.frequencyWhy: On in every level whenever a bounce carries an enemy out of view.
mechanics.summary: While Harvey is in the air, a pixel arrow at the screen edge points at the nearest enemy below or above the view.
how: Set up automatically when any level loads.
Points at the nearest live enemy ahead of Harvey that a bounce has carried above or below the screen, so he can line up the landing.
Z3A2's ghost row has its own chain pointer, which takes priority while it shows.
mechanics.purpose: Keeps stomp chains readable when the camera can't show the next target.
mechanics.presenceNote: Added to every level at runtime; only Z3A2's chain marker is placed in a scene.

mechanics.name: Falling tiles and floating traps
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Placed in 11 build scenes across all four zones.
mechanics.summary: Tiles that shake and glow along a crack when Harvey is near, then drop. Floating traps sweep along fixed paths.
how: A falling tile detects Harvey, shakes in whole pixels with a pulsing orange crack for its warning time, then drops and breaks apart. It hurts on contact.
Floating traps move on patrol paths and hurt on touch.
Respawning puts falling tiles back.
mechanics.purpose: Pushes the player forward and punishes hesitation.

mechanics.name: Zone Select map
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Between every level.
mechanics.summary: An overworld where Harvey walks from node to node. Levels open up to the furthest one reached.
how: Walk along the path between open nodes; Cross / Enter plays the level under Harvey; Circle / Esc goes back to the main menu.
Finishing a level returns to the map with the next one unlocked.
S ranks glow on their nodes.
mechanics.purpose: Shows progress and lets the player replay levels for better ranks.

unlock.text: Opens after choosing a save file.

mechanics.name: Save files and autosave
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Chosen once per session; saves happen on their own.
mechanics.summary: Five save files. Progress, talismans, the Bag, skills and coins are saved automatically.
how: Five slots (slot1-slot5), one active, picked on the main menu and remembered between runs.
Finishing a level, buying a skill and one-time events (like the opening cinematic) autosave.
Arcade runs, the tutorial and greybox prototype scenes are never saved.
mechanics.purpose: Persistence across play sessions.
mechanics.presenceNote: Code-only system; not placed in scenes.

mechanics.name: Skill tree
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Visited between levels when enough crystals have been found.
mechanics.summary: Ten skills on two branches, bought with crystals: Natural Abilities and Talisman Skills. The full tree costs 123 crystals.
how: Natural: Stomp Power I-III (2/4/7), Dash Power I-III (2/4/7), Jump Power I-III (2/4/6), Double Jump (8), Combo Mastery I-IV (3/5/7/9).
Talisman: Chi Focus I-II (3/6), Lasting Charms I-II (3/6), Quick Recharge I-II (2/5), Sky Leap I-II (4/8), Chi Flow I-III (3/5/8).
Each skill needs its parent first (Dash and Jump Power need Stomp Power; Double Jump needs Jump Power II; Combo Mastery needs Dash Power).
Buying a level autosaves. The tutorial ignores bought skills and lends Jump Power III and Double Jump.
mechanics.purpose: The long-term build: it turns gems from chests into stronger stomps, dashes, jumps and combos.

unlock.text: Open from the start; every skill costs crystals.

mechanics.presenceNote: Menu and code; not placed in scenes.

mechanics.name: Gems and crystals
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Gems come out of chests, so a few per level.
mechanics.summary: Jade, Lapis, Topaz and Ruby gems are worth 1, 2, 3 and 5 crystals. Paying cashes the cheapest first and keeps the change.
how: Gems go into the Bag when a chest gives one.
Paying for a skill cashes gems from the cheapest up; the change stays as a crystal balance, so nothing is lost.
mechanics.purpose: The skill tree's currency.
mechanics.presenceNote: Comes from chest rolls, not placed objects.

mechanics.name: Super Jump
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Needed for some high ledges once learned (ledges built for about 2.6 tiles need Jump Power II).
mechanics.summary: Tap jump twice, quickly: the second tap boosts the rising jump into a Super Jump. Jump Power raises it; Sky Leap adds Gale and Comet trails.
how: A second press soon after a jump off the ground, while still rising, boosts the jump so it peaks where a Super Jump from the same take-off would.
Jump Power I-III: take-off x1.25 / 1.5 / 1.65, that is 56% / 125% / 172% higher. Sky Leap I-II adds 6% / 12% and the Gale / Comet take-off effects.
It plays its own take-off animation with a dust ring and spark trail. Jump Power II clears the whole Forest Spirit Fox boss.
mechanics.purpose: Reaching high ledges and jumping clean over bosses.

unlock.text: Jump Power I (2 crystals; needs Stomp Power I).

mechanics.presenceNote: A player skill; not placed in scenes.

mechanics.name: Forest Spirit Fox (enemy)
mechanics.frequencyWhy: The only regular enemy in Grassy Green, the first zone; it is in all five Grass acts.
mechanics.summary: Patrols until it sees Harvey ahead on its level, then crouches, glows green and charges at where he was.
how: Line of sight: in front of it, within range, about on its level, and nothing solid in between.

Telegraph: it stops, crouches and glows spirit green with leaf motes. Charge: it runs at Harvey's last spot with green afterimages, stopping at walls and ledges. Recover: it pants, then patrols again after a cooldown.
Stomps and dashes beat it at any time; from above is never a trigger.
mechanics.purpose: Teaches reading tells and stomping from above in the opening zone.

mechanics.name: Ghoul (ghost enemy)
mechanics.frequencyWhy: In all six Old Tomb acts.
mechanics.summary: The Tomb's purple ghoul. Harvey passes straight through it: it still hurts, but it can't push, block or pin him.
how: Touching it hurts as normal but gives no knockback.
Drawn with the ghost material: translucent shimmering body, purple halo, green eyes and flames.
Stomp or dash it like any enemy.
mechanics.purpose: A hazard that tests timing rather than blocking the way.

mechanics.name: Samurai monkey
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Japan's first two acts.
mechanics.summary: When Harvey comes close on its level and it faces him, it winds up and dashes with a wide slice. From the front it blocks the Spirit Dash.
how: Its slash triggers on line of sight from the front, whichever way Harvey faces; coming from above or behind never triggers it.
A Spirit Dash into its front is blocked: blades clang, Harvey is knocked back without losing health and stunned for 1 s. From behind or above, the dash or a stomp beats it.
It leaves red afterimages on its dash.
mechanics.purpose: Forces stomps from above or attacks from behind instead of dashing through everything.

mechanics.name: Poison pools
mechanics.frequencyWhy: In five of the six Old Tomb acts.
mechanics.summary: The Tomb's purple toxic liquid is instant death, unless Water Breathing is running, which lets Harvey swim in it.
how: Without Water Breathing, touching it kills outright, whatever health or invincibility he has, including when the talisman runs out while he is in it.
With it, the pool acts as water: floaty movement, no breath used, and Jump becomes a swim stroke upwards.
Bubbles pop on the surface and fumes rise off it.
mechanics.purpose: Makes the starting Water Breathing talisman matter in the Old Tomb.

mechanics.name: Water and breath
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Where a level has water (any trigger tagged Water: the Sandy Dunes water zones, and poison with Water Breathing).
mechanics.summary: In water Harvey floats and sinks slowly. With his head under, a bubble meter counts down his breath; at zero he loses health every few seconds.
how: Body in water: lower gravity, a capped sinking speed and slower walking.
Head under: breath runs down one bubble at a time; at zero he takes damage every few seconds until he surfaces.
Underwater: rising bubbles and muffled music and effects.
mechanics.purpose: A slower, floatier space that the Water Breathing talisman opens up.
mechanics.presenceNote: PlayerWater is on the player in every level, so scene presence can't show which levels have water.

mechanics.name: Water Breathing talisman
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Needed for the Tomb's poison pits and long dives.
mechanics.summary: Breathe underwater for 10 seconds at 2.5 chi per second. Harvey glows aqua and wears a bubble helmet.
how: Pauses the breath meter (trait WaterBreathing) and lets Harvey swim in poison.
It is blocked in Z4A6, the first level.
mechanics.purpose: Opens poison and water routes.

unlock.text: Equipped from a new game (starting loadout).

mechanics.name: Villages and shops
mechanics.frequencyWhy: One village per zone on the route.
mechanics.summary: Each zone has a village with a shop counter that sells food and items for coins, and villagers to talk to.
how: Standing at a counter shows a prompt; Up / E opens the shop, which sells the catalogue's village stock for coins.
Villagers answer Up / E with a conversation (see Dialogue).
The town exit returns to the zone map with the next level unlocked.
mechanics.purpose: Somewhere to spend coins and a breather between action levels.

mechanics.name: Quick item
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Used when health or chi runs low.
mechanics.summary: One usable item from the Bag is set as the quick item and used with L1 or Q without opening the Bag.
how: In the Bag, Square / R sets the selected item as the quick item.
A small round plate in the bottom-left corner shows its icon, count and button.
mechanics.purpose: Fast healing or chi in the middle of a fight.

unlock.text: Always available once an item is set.

mechanics.presenceNote: Added to the menus canvas at runtime.

mechanics.name: Healing Stone
mechanics.frequencyWhy: A big chi spend (6 of 9 units), so used a few times a level at most.
mechanics.summary: Spends 60 chi to refill Harvey's health, then shields him from every kind of damage for 7 seconds.
how: Pays 60 chi up front (cheaper up the combo ladder, free at the rainbow stage) and fills the health bar over 1.2 s, one segment at a time.
For 7 s nothing hurts him: enemies, bosses, spikes, kill planes, traps, poison and drowning. A pit lifts him to safe ground. It keeps regenerating a segment at intervals while the shield lasts.
It can be used at full health just for the shield. Cooldown 4 s.
mechanics.purpose: A comeback tool and a way through damage-heavy sections.

unlock.text: Beat the Old Tomb boss (the Void Shrine).

mechanics.notes: The asset's unlock hint still reads "Defeat the Grave Warden in the Old Tomb"; the Void Shrine replaced the Grave Warden on 22 Oct.

mechanics.name: Summoning Talisman
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Chi-limited; used for stretches of a level.
mechanics.summary: Summons the mount assigned to it: the Spirit Fox (faster running, higher leaps) or the dragon (free flight). R1 switches which.
how: Up to 45 s at 3 chi per second, or until chi runs out. Press again, or R2, to get off.
R1 switches the assigned mount between the Spirit Fox and the dragon.
The Spirit Fox runs at 1.6x and jumps 1.15x higher; the dragon flies in any direction and burns 10 chi per second (scaled by the combo stage).
mechanics.purpose: Speed, height and flight for long stretches, paid for in chi.

unlock.text: Beat the Sandy Dunes boss (the Landshark).

mechanics.notes: The asset's unlock hint still reads "Defeat the Sandscale Scarab"; the Landshark replaced it as the Sandy Dunes boss on 27 Oct. The scene's reward (TalismanUnlock in Z2BossSandy) is correct.

mechanics.name: Forest Spirit Fox (Grassy Green boss)
mechanics.frequencyWhy: One fight, the end of the first zone.
mechanics.summary: A giant antlered fox. It charges with its own run cycle, rush-stomps shockwaves along the floor and fires a spirit beam from its antlers.
how: Charge: braces, crouches, then runs the arena; Recover afterwards.
RushStomp: sprints a short way, rears up and slams its front paws down, sending a shockwave each way along the floor.
SpiritBeam: sparks gather at the antlers before the beam.
Openings follow the shared boss rules; a Super Jump with Jump Power II clears its whole body.
mechanics.purpose: The first boss: teaches openings and jumping attacks.

mechanics.name: Void Shrine (Old Tomb boss)
mechanics.frequencyWhy: One fight, the end of the Old Tomb.
mechanics.summary: An antlered fox-skull octopus. It sweeps the floor with a tentacle, throws spirit orbs and, from stage 2, bursts tentacle pillars out of the floor.
how: Tentacle swipe: a pink band flickers along the floor first; only the band near the floor hurts, so jump it. A miss leaves it slumped: the opening.
Projectile: it rises, turns its tail to Harvey and throws green spirit orbs at him, more each stage.
Summon (stage 2 on): glowing cracks mark where pillars burst up, the first always under Harvey. Jumping doesn't clear them; move.
Three lives, one stage each.
mechanics.purpose: A boss about reading floor tells and positioning.

mechanics.name: Sandfin (Sandy Dunes mini-boss)
mechanics.frequencyWhy: One fight, between Act 3 and Act 4 of the Sandy Dunes.
mechanics.summary: A green shark that swims through the sand with only its fin showing, then leaps out of swelling mounds and lunges.
how: Leap: the floor swells into a mound where Harvey stands, then it bursts up through it. Get off the mound.
Lunge: a smaller mound beside Harvey, a red flash and a glint on its teeth, then a short dash and a snap.
Frenzy (last life): double leaps and a lunge that turns into a leap. Misses leave it belly-up: the opening.
Three lives over two stages; no heal.
mechanics.purpose: A smaller rehearsal of the Landshark's sand-swimming rules.

mechanics.name: Landshark (Sandy Dunes boss)
mechanics.frequencyWhy: One fight, the end of the Sandy Dunes.
mechanics.summary: A huge shark that hunts under the sand, breaches in arcs, torpedoes across the arena, snaps in combos and drags Harvey toward a sand whirlpool.
how: Hunt: only its harmless fin shows; a sand mound swells where it will burst out. Stage 2 breaches twice, stage 3 three times.
Charge: a torpedo run along a flickering lane; only the low fin cuts, so jump it. A miss rams the wall: the opening.
BiteCombo (stage 2 on) and Devour (stage 3: a whirlpool pull toward an eruption).
Buried Regeneration heals it (see Boss heals). Four lives over three stages.
mechanics.purpose: The Sandy Dunes finale; the sand hides the boss, so the tells carry the fight.

mechanics.name: Sumaria (Japan boss)
mechanics.frequencyWhy: One fight, the end of the Japan zone.
mechanics.summary: A samurai who charges a full-width dash slash behind a crimson trail, teleports behind Harvey, throws slash waves and rains blades.
how: Stage 1: a charging dash slash, telegraphed by a red glow and a dashed line at blade height; jump it. A miss crashes him into the far wall, dazed: the opening. Attacking while he charges is countered.
Stage 2 adds the teleport slash and slash waves (low: jump; high: stay down). Stage 3 adds blade rain marked on the floor.
Mokuso (stage 2 on): he kneels to heal; while his eyes are closed a hit breaks his focus.
Five lives.
mechanics.purpose: The final zone boss; the hardest reading test in the game.

mechanics.name: Double Jump
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Once learned it is available on every jump; levels don't require it.
mechanics.summary: Press jump in mid-air for a second, slightly lower jump. Not while swimming.
how: After leaving the ground (and its coyote time), one extra jump at 0.9x the normal strength. It comes back on landing.
Not while swimming, dazed or knocked back.
mechanics.purpose: Recovering a missed jump and reaching side routes.

unlock.text: Double Jump (8 crystals; needs Jump Power II).

mechanics.presenceNote: A player skill; not placed in scenes.

mechanics.name: Combo stages 2-4 (Combo Mastery)
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Reached in dash chains and stomp chains once learned.
mechanics.summary: Each Combo Mastery level opens the next combo stage: orange, hot pink, violet, then rainbow. Higher stages bring bigger effects and cheaper chi.
how: Combo Mastery I-IV (3/5/7/9 crystals) raises the stage cap from 1 to 5.
Each stage adds motes, faster glow pulses and stronger hit effects (falling sparks from stage 2, speed lines from stage 4).
Talisman costs drop with the stage (60%, 35%, 15%, 5%, free).
mechanics.purpose: Makes long chains pay off in chi and spectacle.

unlock.text: Combo Mastery I-IV (needs Dash Power I).

mechanics.presenceNote: Runtime combo and skill; not placed in scenes.

mechanics.name: Living and spirit worlds
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Throughout Japan's first acts, its village and the boss arena.
mechanics.summary: In Japan, tori gates switch between the living world and the spirit world, each with its own platforms, coins and enemies.
how: Passing a tori gate flips the world; objects belonging to the other world (tiles, coins, enemies, bounce boxes, backgrounds) switch on or off.
The spirit world gets a cool colour shift and the switch a screen ripple.
mechanics.purpose: Japan's signature puzzle-platforming layer.

mechanics.name: Tomb darkness
mechanics.frequencyWhy: On in every Old Tomb level.
mechanics.summary: The Old Tomb is dark, lit by a flickering circle of light around Harvey and around torches, lamps and checkpoints.
how: A darkness overlay covers the camera view in Z1 levels, with light circles at Harvey and light sources.
Kept light enough that the level stays readable.
mechanics.purpose: Atmosphere and a sense of exploration in the Tomb.
mechanics.presenceNote: Added by ZoneAtmosphere at runtime in Z1 levels.

mechanics.name: Rolling boulder
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Two Old Tomb levels.
mechanics.summary: Step past a shaft in the ceiling and, after a rumble and trickling grit, a boulder drops and rolls after Harvey.
how: Triggers once when Harvey is a set distance to one side of the shaft: a rumble, grit and a small shake, then the drop.
No cutscene and no camera change: Harvey keeps control and has to outrun it.
Respawning resets it.
mechanics.purpose: A set-piece chase.

mechanics.name: Spirit Fox mount
mechanics.frequencyWhy: When the Summoning Talisman is set to the fox.
mechanics.summary: Harvey rides the Spirit Fox: faster running, higher leaps, its own run cycle that matches his speed.
how: The fox materialises from a pixel dissolve with a leafy aura and a ring of leaves.
1.6x run speed and 1.15x jump; a Spirit Dash on it keeps its own speed rather than stacking.
Its run loop plays at Harvey's speed and holds a leaping frame in the air.
mechanics.purpose: A speed and height boost for long runs.
mechanics.presenceNote: On the player prefab, so it is in every level; that says nothing about how often it is used.

mechanics.name: Dragon flight
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Chi-limited flight, when the Summoning Talisman is set to the dragon.
mechanics.summary: Harvey's dragon carries him in free flight in any direction until chi runs out, leaving golden motes.
how: Summoned with a cream flash, a golden aura, a screen ripple and a spark ring.
Both stick axes steer; flight burns 10 chi per second, scaled by the combo stage, and is free at the rainbow stage.
Chi running out ends the flight.
mechanics.purpose: Skipping hazards and exploring, paid for in chi.
mechanics.presenceNote: On the player prefab, so it is in every level; that says nothing about how often it is used.

mechanics.name: Dash Clash
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Only when Harvey's dash meets a samurai monkey's dash head-on.
mechanics.summary: When Harvey's Spirit Dash meets the samurai monkey's dash head-on, the two cancel: the world goes black and 「戦い」 ("battle") flashes up.
how: The exception to the samurai's block: dash meets dash and neither takes damage or knockback.
A short hit-stop (time scale 0.15 for 0.12 s), the background goes black behind the two fighters, and the battle card fades back in about half a second.
mechanics.purpose: A rewarding flourish for meeting the samurai head-on with perfect timing.

mechanics.name: Boss heals
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Two bosses, two tries a fight each.
mechanics.summary: The Landshark and Sumaria can win a life back mid-fight, but each heal has a counter.
how: Only from stage 2, at least one life down, two attempts per fight, with a cooldown; a heal never drops the boss's stage.
Landshark: Buried Regeneration, dives away from Harvey to heal under the sand.
Sumaria: Mokuso, kneels with closed eyes while petals spiral in; a hit while his eyes are closed breaks it. Once they open, zanshin counters.
mechanics.purpose: Punishes passive play late in the fight.

mechanics.name: Chi Flow
mechanics.frequencyWhy: During any combo of 3+ hits, once learned.
mechanics.summary: While a combo of 3 or more hits lasts, chi flows back: a unit every 5, 3 or 2 seconds.
how: Chi Flow I-III (3/5/8 crystals; needs Quick Recharge).
mechanics.purpose: Lets a skilled player keep dashing on chi earned by chaining.
mechanics.presenceNote: A player skill; not placed in scenes.

mechanics.name: Rainbow Combo stage
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Needs Combo Mastery IV and five quick hits; the dash-chain sections can hold it for a while.
mechanics.summary: The fifth combo stage. Harvey's outline cycles every colour, talismans and the dragon cost no chi, nearby coins fly to him and the music changes.
how: Reached at stage 5, which only Combo Mastery IV opens.
Chi costs drop to zero (Chi.StageCost), so dashes, healing and flight are free while it lasts.
Coins within 4.5 units slide to Harvey (the pull the Coin Magnet used), and the level music switches while the stage lasts (RAINBOWMUSIC).
Stars rise off Harvey, every hit throws confetti, and a second swirl of motes turns the other way.
mechanics.purpose: The payoff for mastering the combo, and the game's most striking visual state.
mechanics.presenceNote: Runtime combo state; Z4A8's long Spirit Fox line is the clearest place to reach it.

mechanics.name: Challenge rooms
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Two rooms, in Z4A6 and Z4A7.
mechanics.summary: Rooms that lock when Harvey walks in and release him after five rounds of enemies, with a restoring reward chest.
how: Z4A6's cave closes its ways out with the level's own rock; Z4A7's side chamber switches off the Jump Mushroom under its only exit.
Each round spawns more enemies one by one, marked by spirit wisps first; a banner shows the round and enemies left.
Win: the way out opens and a chest with a Spirit Peach and Chi Crystals drops in, once. Lose: the enemies vanish and the room can be tried again.
mechanics.purpose: An optional combat test in the opening zone.

mechanics.name: Villager dialogue
mechanics.frequencyWhy: In the four villages.
mechanics.summary: Villagers talk in a text box in the HUD style, with typed-out lines and choices picked with the paw pointer.
how: Up / E next to a villager on the ground starts their conversation.
Cross / Enter / E shows the whole line then goes on; Up/Down picks a choice; Circle / Esc leaves. The game pauses while it is open.
mechanics.purpose: Story and flavour between levels.

mechanics.name: Basic Controls tutorial
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Played once, from the main menu, if at all.
mechanics.summary: A short level that teaches move, jump, stomp, Super Jump and dash one step at a time, then all of them together.
how: A plate at the top shows each step with keyboard and controller buttons; meeting the step's goals moves on.
Only the Spirit Dash is equipped; it lends Jump Power III and Double Jump; chi never runs out; nothing is saved.
mechanics.purpose: Onboarding.

mechanics.name: Biplane crash opening
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Once per save file.
mechanics.summary: The game's opening: Harvey flies his biplane over the meadow, the engine fails, and he crash-lands under the cliff where the level begins.
how: Arrival, engine trouble (backfires and smoke), the dive, the impact (dust, sparks, shake) and Harvey climbing out of the level's own wreck.
Plays once per save file and is skipped in arcade and tutorial runs and for files already past the level. Jump skips it.
mechanics.purpose: Sets up the story and the first level in one shot.

unlock.text: A new save file's first level (Z4A6).

mechanics.name: Arcade run
mechanics.frequencyWhy: A separate way to start; not part of a saved playthrough.
mechanics.summary: An unsaved run from the first level with a new-game loadout.
how: Started from the main menu's arcade entry (MenueControl.StartArcade).
Nothing is saved, and the opening cinematic is skipped.
mechanics.purpose: Quick play without touching save files.
mechanics.notes: The code path exists; whether the current main menu shows an Arcade button wasn't checked in the scene for this catalogue.

mechanics.name: Coin Magnet talisman
mechanics.frequencyWhy: Status unclear (see the note).
mechanics.summary: For 8 seconds every coin nearby flies to Harvey. Awarded by Sumaria's arena, but it isn't in the talisman catalogue.
how: 8 s, cooldown 6 s, 1.25 chi per second, radius 4.5, pull speed 7.
Z3BossBattle's TalismanUnlock gives this talisman on Sumaria's defeat.
mechanics.purpose: Coin collection.
mechanics.notes: Not listed in HNLCatalog.talismans, which save files use to turn talisman ids back into assets, and CoinAttractor's comments say the pull was taken out of the talisman for "whatever replaces the Coin Magnet talisman later". Whether the reward survives a save, or the talisman is being retired, needs a decision.
